recordedOn: Apple M4 Max, macOS 26.5.2, Node 22.23.1 (the flake devShell's node — the version CI runs; recorded with `nix develop --command pnpm bench --update-baseline`). Each figure is the median of FIVE whole-benchmark runs, not one.
note: guards are slow/fast A/B ratios measured in one process against one data set: the machine cancels, so these are the real gate (tolerance 1.30, except the shipped-vs-frozen gate at 1.15). workloads are workload/yardstick ratios and are only approximately machine-independent — indicative, not authoritative (tolerance 2.0). Observed spread across the five recording runs: guards 3-8% EXCEPT neighbour-read/shipped-vs-frozen-inline-reference at 25% (0.879 to 1.124), which is the one guard carrying the TIGHT 1.15 tolerance — its lowest observed run sits only 3% above its own failure threshold, so it is the first thing to suspect in a red run and the harness header's claim of 5-6% spread for it does not reproduce. workloads 6-10%. ON NODE VERSIONS: the same benchmark on Node 24.13.0 puts the workload ratios 22-32% above these and the HashSet guards 16-18% above them. The recorded environment is Node 22; comparing across major versions is not meaningful. Regenerate with `pnpm bench --update-baseline` and say in the commit message what moved and why.
